paper_role: architecture redesign after the frozen single-NEFF precision-composition gate failed
motivation: The single cache_skip_step NEFF is bit-exact to a fused FP32 predictor-to-Euler reference, but not to the current predictor contract that rounds to BF16 before scheduling. A ranked NEFF boundary is introduced to preserve that semantic cast without host materialization.

frozen_system.schedule: FLUX.1-dev 50-step dynamically shifted FlowMatch Euler sigmas
skip_path: cache_predict(two FP32 coefficients) -> BF16 ranked device tensor
cache_scheduler_step(ranked prediction, FP32 delta sigma) -> aliased BF16 latent

gates.S1_exact_contract: All 50 latent states and final latent must be bit-exact to predictor-BF16-round followed by FlowMatch Euler.
gates.S2_zero_host_materialization: All 38 ranked predictor-to-scheduler handoffs must have zero full-tensor host writes and reads.
gates.S3_scalar_control: A skip may write only two coefficients and delta sigma from host; a scalar checksum read is allowed for synchronized timing.

scope_limit: This split experiment still uses host-originated synthetic actual-noise tensors on anchor steps; real backbone ranked ingress and end-to-end speed remain unproven.

decision.if_pass: Adopt the split predictor/scheduler boundary as the exact H1c cache-step contract and connect the real FLUX backbone.
decision.if_fail: Preserve the single-NEFF fused numerical contract only as an explicitly different cache algorithm, or stop resident composition.
